description: UrbanHeatPro is a Python bottom-up model for hourly space-heating and hot-water demand in an urban building stock. Its README documents a CSV input for building area, use, construction-year class and exposed walls, with configurable time resolution and demand-side measures such as renovation and night setback. Users supply a study-area building list and weather or scenario assumptions; outputs are heat-demand profiles from individual buildings up to a city. Default characteristic values are based on German statistics. GitHub metadata states GPL-3.0 licensing. A limitation is that non-residential hot-water demand is not calculated in the documented version, and default German typologies need checking before use elsewhere. The model can produce district-heating demand and retrofit scenarios for urban energy simulations. The catalogue's EnergyPlus model offers more detailed individual-building physics, while this repository focuses on stock-level demand. No building list, weather data or model package was downloaded.
inputs: Building-stock CSV, typology and weather assumptions
name: UrbanHeatPro urban heat-demand model
